title: Deploy Field Lifecycle — weekly debrief and install experiments
content:
Purpose: quick field-week debrief capturing experiments, recurring customer blockers, and action items so SE, SRE, and install squads can align.

Summary highlights:
- Ran an experiment with delta-based NFS mounting to reduce cold-start time for on-prem KV-cache recovery (customer: Meridian Financial). Median cold-start reduced ~23% in test, but two customers saw intermittent permission errors.
- Continued recurring pattern of customer firewall policies blocking inter-node GRPC on port 7002 after subnet migration. Root cause: managed VPN appliances rewriting TCP MSS on IPsec tunnels.
- Successfully exercised KMS-backed cert rotation in a staging VPC for Zenith (on-prem air-gapped) — found UX gap in console that caused the rotation to stall when HSM SLA exceeded 500ms.
- Canary rollout of quantized-2-byte model variant for a Dedicated customer showed 8–12% cost savings, but inference-quality regression on long-context prompts for one eval set.

This week’s standup notes (03–10 Oct 2026):
2026-10-03 — Tue
- Meridian Financial install: Diego + Marcus. Observed NFS permission errors after node reboots; suspected umask mismatch + stale NFSv4 state. Workaround: restart nfsd + remount; permanent fix: upgrade mount flags and add a pre-reboot flush job. Ticket PD-4127 opened.
- Customer-network triage with Zenith: found IPsec tunnel MSS clamping on their Palo Alto edge appliance — causes GRPC segmentation when payloads > 14KB. Temporary mitigation: enable path-mtu-discovery and set gRPC KEEPALIVE to 20s. Long-term: add MSS detection in the install preflight check.
- Private console: observed cert-rotation UI timeout when HSM latency high. Repro steps in linked PR. Owner: Sofia to draft UX fallback (rotate via CLI) by 2026-10-07.

2026-10-05 — Thu
- Offsite install for AtlasHealth: initial bootstrap failed due to dropped SSH key acceptance on firstboot (their bastion had overly strict RHEL lockfile). Root cause: bootstrap script raced with cloud-init; fix: add retry loop + jitter. Patch in PR linked.
- KV-cache warmup experiment: running candidate script to prepopulate LRU windows using synthetic traces. Results: 18% fewer cold-cache misses but add ~2s to initial request in worst-case. Need to evaluate SLO tradeoff.
- Canary quantized model: flagged quality regression on long-context summarization prompts (eval set: PD-4189). Action: Research to profile where quantization loses context fidelity (Sofia + Applied ML).

Open/blocking customer issues:
- GRPC segmentation after subnet changes (two customers). Blocking because application UX shows dropped responses, leads to customer rollback risk. Workarounds documented; engineering to add a preflight network check (MSS, iptables, NAT behavior). Owner: Marcus Li, ETA: 2026-10-12.
- Stalled cert rotations in air-gapped HSMs (one customer). This is an escalated support case with security team involved. Need an emergency CLI escape hatch that avoids the console path and exposes detailed HSM timings. Owner: Sofia, in coordination with Security.
- Intermittent NFS v4 permission failures after reboot (Meridian). Blocking some installs; mitigation applied but needs a release-grade fix. Owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-10-11.

Action items (concrete):
- PD-4127: add nfs mount flag change + pre-reboot flush job; test matrix across RHEL 8/9 and Ubuntu 22.04. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-10-11.
- Network preflight: implement MSS/path-mtu detection in installer and fail fast with clear remediation steps. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2026-10-12.
- Cert rotation CLI fallback: implement CLI rotate-cert --force-without-hsm-timeout and expose detailed HSM latency logs to console. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-10-07 (prototype) / 2026-10-14 (release).
- KV-cache warmup opt-in flag for on-prem installs; add metric telemetry for warmup hit-rate. Owner: Anika. Due: 2026-10-18.
- Quantization regression triage: run epoch-level signal tracking and create small eval harness around long-context summarization test. Owner: Sofia + Applied ML (Marcel Chen). Due: 2026-10-15.

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Consider adding an "edge network diagnostics" container that runs on first-boot and submits a short report to support (ttl-signed) — lightweight, no telemetry upload by default.
- Investigate if customers with managed VPN appliances (Palo Alto / Cisco ASA) have consistent MSS clamping rules — might become a doc/KB article.
- Follow up with dedicated infra about introducing an infra-level gRPC healthcheck that tolerates path-mtu issues by doing smaller initial probes.

Runbook tweaks proposed (short bullets):
- Installer preflight: new checks for (a) ability to open 7001–7005 TCP, (b) MTU/MSS sanity, (c) NFSv4 state tests with remount simulation.
- Support KB: add troubleshooting checklist for "stalled cert rotation" with HSM latency dump command.
- Release notes: mark KV-cache warmup as opt-in for now and include perf tradeoffs.

Risks & decisions needed:
- Decision: enable KV warmup by default? (Risk: increases initial request latency; Benefit: fewer cold misses). Need a business-level SLO discussion — schedule with product.
- Risk: adding installer preflight increases pre-deploy time; but reduces in-field debugging. Consider parallelizing checks.

Meeting attendees / syncs this week:
- Tuesday triage: Diego, Marcus, Sofia, Anika.
- Zenit customer sync: Sofia, Customer Success (Liam Park), Security (Nora Chen).
- AtlasHealth postmortem: Diego, Infra Eng (Priya Rao).

Quick decisions made in meeting:
- Approve prototype of CLI cert-rotation fallback (Sofia).
- Accept NFS mount-change patch into hotfix branch for Meridian and 1 other at-risk customer (Diego).

Misc notes / snippets for docs:
- "If using site firewall appliances that manipulate MSS, enable path-mtu-discovery on the WAN side and ensure GRE/ESP rules are passthrough for large gRPC messages."
- Example diagnostic command to run on customer host: iperf3 -M 1400 -c <peer> ; ip route get <peer> to show pmtu.

Next check-in cadence: weekly sync on Monday 10/12 09:30 PT (standup + blockers). Recommend adding a 30-minute triage slot on Wednesday for any new escalations.


-- End of debrief --
